title: Directional light + runtime controls + occlusion amplification (debug)
purpose: Introduce an explicit directional light for the mesh path and tools to verify that ray-query occlusion is wired by making the effect highly visible.

steps.detail: Add a global/light UBO or push constants for a directional light: direction (default normalize(-0.5,-0.8,-0.6)), intensity, enable flag. Bind for mesh fragment shader.

In shaders/particle_mesh.frag, compute a simple Lambert/emissive mix: baseColor = fragColor.rgb; N = normalize(camera-facing normal or implicit billboard normal = +Z in view→world); lambert = max(dot(N, -lightDir), 0); finalColor = baseColor * (0.3 + 0.7*lambert).
Apply shadowVis from ray query as a multiplier on the lighting term: finalColor *= mix(1.0, shadowVis, shadowWeight), with shadowWeight default 1.0.
Add a debug toggle 'rtOcclusionAmplify' that, when enabled, sets shadowWeight=2.0 and clamps to [0,1], or simply darkens more aggressively (e.g., square the visibility).
Add keyboard controls: J/K to adjust light theta, H/N to adjust light phi, U/I to increase/decrease intensity, O to toggle occlusion amplify. Print current values every 1s while adjusting.

acceptance: With RT enabled and amplify toggle ON, clear darkening is visible when occluders intersect particles
Directional light can be rotated live to move the shadow region
mcp_queries: search_vulkan_spec('descriptor updates and image layout consistency')
notes: Keep RT toggle path intact. Initial normal for particles can be approximated; for billboards use view-facing normal.
